original_record.Case Information: A man in his 20s presented to the emergency department with 1 day of chest pressure. Four days prior to presentation he experienced subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, a dry cough, and sinus congestion. The day prior to presentation he experienced 3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously. In the early morning of the day of presentation, he was awakened from sleep by constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw, diaphoresis, and 1 episode of vomiting. He reported no medical history.
original_record.Physical Examination: Vital signs obtained in the Emergency Department were within normal limits. Cardiac examination revealed a regular rate and rhythm, normal point of maximum impulse without lifts, and no murmurs, rubs, or gallops in supine, sitting, or standing positions. The remainder of the physical examination was within normal limits.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests:
- Laboratory Tests:
  * Initial serum troponin I level: 6.18 ng/mL
  * Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein (values increased over next 3 days)

- Imaging and Other Tests:
  * ECG Findings: Normal sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, ST-segment depression in lead V1, and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR
  * Coronary angiography: Normal coronary arteries, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure 12 mm Hg (reference range, 4-12 mm Hg)
  * Transthoracic echocardiogram: Normal results

original_record.Case Information: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset chest pain. She had no history of any acute febrile illness or family history of sudden cardiac death.
original_record.Physical Examination: Patient was tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min. Her blood pressure was normal.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests: - Laboratory tests:    - White blood cell count: 14,300/µL (normal range: 3500-9500/µL)    - Serum calcium: within normal limits    - High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL (normal range: <0.015 ng/mL)    - Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL (normal range: 0-100 pg/mL)  - ECG findings:    Image Title: Electrocardiograms at Admission and Different Time Points    Image Description: Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6. ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V2 to V6, with ST-segment depression in lead aVR.  - Imaging studies:    - Coronary angiography: revealed normal coronary arteries    - Left ventriculography: confirmed systolic apical ballooning    - Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

original_record.Case Information: A 59-year-old man with a history of hypertension and medication-induced diabetes presented with new-onset heart failure symptoms. The symptoms began 2 weeks after receiving a COVID-19 vaccination booster. The patient had no significant family history. Past medical conditions included hypertension and medication-induced diabetes.
original_record.Physical Examination: Clinical examination revealed signs of volume overload with presence of lower-extremity edema and jugular venous distention.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests: - Laboratory Tests:    * Blood urea nitrogen: 46 mg/dL    * Creatinine: 1.79 mg/dL (estimated glomerular filtration rate: 43 mL/min/1.73 m²)    * Uric acid: 14.1 mg/dL    * N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide: 206 ng/dL    * Negative results for tuberculin skin testing, rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, and viral studies- Imaging Studies:    * Electrocardiogram: PR depressions and inferolateral ST-segment elevation    * Echocardiogram:      - Left ventricular ejection fraction: 64%      - Right ventricular dysfunction (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion: 15 mm)      - Increased inferior vena cava size: 28 mm with reduced inspiratory collapse (<50%)      - Mild tricuspid regurgitation      Image Title: Figure 1      Image Description: Echocardiograph showing reduced inspiratory collapse    * Cardiac MRI:      - Thickened pericardium greater than 40 mm      - Evidence of ventricular interdependence and septal bounce      Image Title: Figure 2      Image Description: Contrast-enhanced axial computed tomography scan showing uniformly thickened pericardium- Cardiac Catheterization Results:    * At rest:      - Right atrial pressure: 15 mm Hg      - Pulmonary artery pressure: 28/17 (mean, 21) mm Hg      - Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure: 16 mm Hg with V-wave of 20      - Cardiac output: 4.08 L/min      - Cardiac index: 1.8 L/min/m²    * During passive exercise:      - Right atrium pressure: 40 mm Hg      - Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure: 50 mm Hg      - Cardiac output: 2.38 L/min      - Cardiac index: 1.02 L/min/m²      - Pulmonary artery saturation declined from 66% to 44%

original_record.Case Information: A 29-year-old woman from the Dominican Republic, who moved to the United States in 2014, presented in January 2016 for prenatal care. A purified protein derivative skin test was positive (21 mm). In January 2022, she was started on rifampin (300 mg daily) for a planned 4-month course. She was taking no other medications. After three months of therapy, she experienced two days of nausea, vomiting, and subjective fevers.
original_record.Physical Examination: Initial presentation showed no significant physical examination findings noted in the case report.

original_record.Case Information: A 52-year-old man presented with sudden, pressure-like, substernal chest pain that started at rest and radiated to the left jaw, associated with nausea, dyspnea, and diaphoresis. Symptoms began approximately 6 hours before arrival. Two hours after intervention, the patient reported a new onset of fever and worsening chest pain that was retrosternal and sharp in quality, but not affected by positional changes or exertion.
original_record.Physical Examination: Initial examination: Patient was tachycardic, with no murmurs. No crackles were present on lung auscultation. Jugular venous pressure was normal. Follow-up examination: Temperature of 38.3°C, auscultation revealed a new pericardial friction rub located over the left sternal border.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests:
- Laboratory Tests:
Initial troponin levels were 14 µg/L

- Imaging Studies:
1. Initial ECG showed ST-segment elevations in leads II, aVF, and V3-V5
2. Coronary angiography findings: acute thrombotic total occlusion of the mid-segment of the left anterior descending artery with TIMI 0 flow. Ventriculography demonstrated an ejection fraction of 55% to 60%
3. Second ECG: complete resolution of ST-segment elevation in V2-V3 with persistence of ST-segment elevation in II, III, aVF, and V4-V6 without reciprocal changes
4. Third ECG (24 hours later): diffuse ST-segment elevation on II, III, aVF, and V3-V5 accompanied by PR-segment depression in I and II and PR-segment elevation in aVR without reciprocal changes
5. Transthoracic echocardiogram: no evidence of pericardial effusion, no wall motion abnormalities, ejection fraction of 55% to 60%

Options.A: Acute coronary syndrome with early post-infarction pericarditis

original_record.Case Information: A 2-year-old girl was involved in a car accident. She was admitted to a local hospital with skull fractures, cerebral contusions, pulmonary contusions, and fractures of the left iliac bone. She was initially stabilized with valproic acid and mannitol. From day 13, she developed repeated high fevers (peak of 39.7°C) that were unresponsive to multiple antibiotics. On day 18, she developed a mild cough without sputum production, wheezing, shortness of breath, or cyanosis.
original_record.Physical Examination: Patient was irritable with a Glasgow coma scale score of 10 (E4V2M4). Bilateral pupils were equally large and reacted sensitively to light. Muscular tension was high in all four limbs. Bilateral Babinski sign was positive. No signs of meningeal irritation. Dark red rashes were present on face, neck, and trunk; some were desquamative, without exudation or hemorrhage. Breath sounds were rough, without wheezing or rales. No significant abnormal signs in cardiac circulation and abdomen.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests: Laboratory Tests:- Liver function: ALT 531 U/L (ref: 7-40), AST 255 U/L (ref: 13-35), GGT 158 U/L (ref: 7-45)- Blood counts: Neutrophils 0.04×10⁹/L (ref: 1.8-6.3), Hemoglobin 76 g/L (ref: 110-140), Platelets 89×10⁹/L (ref: 125-350)- Other markers: Ferritin 1577.9 ng/mL (ref: 4.6-204), PCT mildly elevated (1.24 ng/mL)- Immunological tests showed CD4+/CD8+ T-cell ratio of 2.65 (ref: 1.02-1.94) and low B-cell count (91/μL; ref: 107-698/μL)Imaging and Pathology:- Bone marrow morphology showed diminution of hematopoietic cells, infiltration of lymphocytes and histiocytes- Bone marrow biopsy revealed no fibrosis or malignancy- Initial CT confirmed skull fractures, cerebral contusions, and pulmonary contusionsMicrobiology:- Human metapneumovirus detected in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid- Negative cultures from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, peripheral blood, and urine
original_record.Final Diagnosis: Valproic acid-induced aplastic crisis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome

Options.D: Valproic acid-induced aplastic crisis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome

original_record.Case Information: A 42-year-old Caucasian man with a 12-year history of well-controlled HIV (undetectable viral load, CD4+ count 1184 × 10^6 cell/liter). Past medical history includes treatment for early latent syphilis six years prior. The patient presented with low-grade fever (37.5°) and sudden appearance of skin lesions at the base of his penis. He reported recent sexual activity with multiple male partners. Two days after the initial skin manifestations, he developed fever up to 39°C, chest pain without irradiation, and shortness of breath.
original_record.Physical Examination: Initial examination revealed vesicular and umbilicated lesions on genitals and small lymphadenomegaly in the groin area. No oropharyngeal lesions were detected. Upon admission for chest symptoms, the patient was hemodynamically stable with continuous anterior chest pain exacerbated by deep breathing.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests: - Laboratory Tests:    * High-sensitivity cardiac troponin: 128.00 pg/ml initially, peaked at 142.00 pg/ml (reference value < 14 pg/ml)    * Multiple viral serologies including CMV, EBV, Coxsackievirus, Echovirus, Parvovirus B19, and Herpes virus 1/2 were negative (except for past CMV and EBV exposure)    - Imaging Studies:    * ECG: Showed sinus tachycardia with elevated PR segment in aVR lead and depressed in peripheral and thoracic leads    * Echocardiography: Left ventricle diastolic diameter of 59 mm, hypokinetic left ventricle with EF 50%    * Chest CT angiography: Normal, no pulmonary embolism or pneumonia    * Cardiac MRI: Showed slightly increased global T1 and T2 mapping values, minimal hyperintensity of pericardium without effusion, normal biventricular function (EF 57%)    * Coronary CT angiography: Normal    - Continuous Monitoring:    * ECG monitoring showed persistent episodes of sinus pauses (longest 10.1 seconds)    * Episodes of advanced AV block grade 2 Mobitz type 1 and 2    * Sinus bradycardia (heart rate 40-45, nadir 32 pulses/minute while sleeping)
original_record.Final Diagnosis: Myopericarditis with cardiac conduction system involvement due to monkeypox virus infection with concurrent Lyme disease

Options.C: Myopericarditis with cardiac conduction system involvement due to monkeypox virus infection with concurrent Lyme disease

original_record.Case Information: A 64-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with complaints of hemoptysis, fever, and difficulty exhaling that stretched for five days. The patient had previous history of hypertension and field work.
original_record.Physical Examination: Upon admission:- Temperature: 37.8°C- Respiratory rate: 22/min- Blood pressure: 144/88 mmHg- Dyspnea presentSix hours after initial treatment:- Temperature increased to 40°C- Respiratory rate increased to 28/min- Blood pressure dropped to 80/50 mmHg- Patient required intubation
original_record.Diagnostic Tests: Laboratory Tests:- Complete blood count, liver function, and kidney function tests were performed (specific values available in Table 1)- Blood gas analysis showed type II respiratory failure- Next Generation Sequencing (mNGS) testing performed on blood samplesImaging Studies:1. Initial Chest CT:- Title: High-resolution CT images on admission- Description: Both lungs scattered with exudative lesions2. Chest X-ray Series:- First day: Showed diffuse inflammatory changes in both lungs- Tenth day: Follow-up chest X-ray- Follow-up CT: Showed resolution of exudative fociOther Diagnostic Procedures:- Fibronchoscopy findings: Copious amount of bloody sputum in each lung segment

original_record.Case Information: A 39-year-old female patient with history of endometrial polyp excision, cesarean section, and resolved gestational diabetes mellitus. She was admitted for recurring right upper abdomen pain due to cholelithiasis and cholecystitis for five years. Three months before admission, she experienced persistent cramping discomfort in upper right quadrant with nausea and retching after high-fat meals. Pain radiated to back but was relieved with antibiotics. No family history of similar conditions. Patient had normal blood pressure and no symptoms except occasional sudden upper abdomen pain.
original_record.Physical Examination: 6 hours post-cholecystectomy: Patient showed lucid consciousness but mental tiredness, pale face and cyanotic lips. Vital signs: Heart rate 135 BPM, blood pressure 140/80 mmHg, respiratory rate 44 BPM, oxygen saturation 80-85%. Auscultation revealed crackling noises in all areas of right lung and lower parts of left lung. Heart examination showed tachycardia and bigeminal beats.
original_record.Diagnostic Tests:
- Laboratory Tests:
  - Arterial blood gas: pH 7.182, PO2 59.1 mmHg, PCO2 30.4 mmHg, HCO3- 11.0 mmol/L, BE -16.3 mmol/L, lactic acid 6.8 mmol/L
  - NT-proBNP: 845 pg/mL
  - White blood cell count: 28.10 × 10^9/L
  - Hemoglobin: 10.9 g/dL
  - Elevated liver enzymes: ALT 603 U/L
  - Elevated pancreatic enzymes: Lipase 191 U/L, Amylase 327 U/L
  - Renal function: BUN 165.6 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL

- Imaging Studies:
  - CT scan: Left adrenal mass measuring 26 × 25 × 31mm
  Image Title: Adrenal contrast-enhanced CT
  Image Description: Left adrenal region measuring approximately 26 × 25 mm, with CT value 37 Hounsfield units

  - Chest CT: Diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates, right side more severe
  Image Title: Post-cholecystectomy chest CT
  Image Description: DAH with right side particularly evident

- Other Tests:
  - ECG: Frequent ventricular premature beats, shortened PR interval, substantial ST depression, inverted T waves
  - Bronchoscopy: Abundant pale, red, thin secretions in both airways, particularly right airway
original_record.Final Diagnosis: Pheochromocytoma presenting as left adrenal incidentaloma with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage

Options.B: Pheochromocytoma presenting as left adrenal incidentaloma with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Options.C: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)/diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
